writeCapDoReqPerGB.unit: write-cap counter requests per GB written
writeCapDoReqPerGB.how: The lab's gbDoReq: all of it is the optional daily write cap's counter (the verifier), so it counts only with the cap on. An upper bound: other runs shared the counter in those minutes; the code path gives about 122 per GB. Same runs: requests to the deployment's write-cap counter room (one reserve per write call) in the upload phase's minutes, per 1e9 bytes; an upper bound (the counter is shared, and other runs' keyframe writes in those minutes count too; the code path gives 1 per part + 2, about 121 per GB); 0 without the cap.

editArchiveRowsWritten.how: Once a project passes 10,000 changes, each old change moves to a compressed archive file and its row is deleted; Cloudflare bills a delete as a row written (room.ts, the pricing page). Not measured: the lab's runs never reached 10,000 changes.

changeBytes.how: A change row's size in the room's database until it's archived: an estimate from the row layout, not measured.

replicaRowsWritten.how: From the verifier's fit over 81 edit runs (rows = 64.5 + 2 × parties + 1.025 × edits, no residual): a person's first push to a project writes 2 rows once. Not a separate input in the lab's file.

upkeepAlarmPerHour.how: The room's upkeep (archiving old changes, sweeping expired envelopes) is due an hour after an edit or a hello: at most one an editing hour per project (room.ts). Priced like a presence-check alarm. Not measured.

writeCapRowsPerReserve.how: Only with the daily write cap on: each reserve writes a row in the counter's room (the verifier, from write-cap.ts); no lab input carries it.

pvoViewClassBPerSegment.how: Optimized: a read GETs each segment's list entry and its bytes from R2, 2 Class B a segment, by the read path the first preview re-check verified at 2 and 4 MiB (CF-VERIFY-PROXY.md). Not measured at the release's 1 MiB reads.

pvoViewClassBPerRead.how: Optimized: each read also GETs the next list entry past its byte budget (and the end at the edge): 1 Class B a read, by the same verified read path. Not measured at 1 MiB reads.

segVaultDoReq.how: Before the fix, without R2: a segment's 3 writes, the damage check and 2 heads go to the vault: 6 vault requests (the lab's request structure per segment, measured on R2). Not measured on the vault.

pvoSegVaultDoReq.how: Optimized, without R2: an append writes its part's 3 objects to the vault: about 3 vault requests a segment. Not measured on the vault.

segVaultRowsWritten.how: Without R2, a segment is 3 objects (bytes, manifest, list entry), each a record row and a 1 MiB chunk row (blob-do.ts); deleting it later costs the same. Not measured on the vault.

viewVaultDoReqPerSegment.how: Without R2, a segment played is 3 signed reads (list entry, manifest, bytes), each one request to the vault (the lab's read structure per segment, measured on R2). Not measured on the vault.

pvoViewVaultDoReqPerSegment.how: Optimized, without R2: a batched read gets each segment's list entry and bytes: 2 vault requests a segment. Not measured on the vault.

viewVaultRowsReadPerSegment.how: Without R2, each of a segment's 3 objects reads its record row and its 1 MiB chunk row (blob-do.ts); a segment over 1 MiB reads a chunk row per MiB. Not measured on the vault.

viewVaultGBsPerMiB.how: Without R2, the vault is awake about 80 ms per MiB it serves: an estimate, not measured.

limits.value: 10 ms of CPU per request on Workers Free (on Paid, 5 minutes: it doesn't apply in practice)
limits.observed: Appends and reads stay under 10 ms apart from a few, mostly a stream's first media append or a client's first read. 8 of 255 were at or over 10 ms (max 23 ms), and none were refused (no 1102 on any Worker that day). Typical: an append 3.915 ms, a 1 MiB read 3.182 ms (cf-verify4, 3 runs on 4G).
limits.carton: The release keeps every preview request small: one part (1 MiB) per append and 1 MiB reads, the limits the server advertises, with 4 appends and 2 reads in flight to keep the speed. On Workers Paid the limit is 5 minutes a request.

limits.observed: Before fix/cf-stream-parts, a part upload read its 8-64 MiB body into JS: 61-359 ms CPU per part; after a burst Cloudflare killed them (exceededCpu, error 1102, HTTP 503). A 1 GB upload to R2 never completed (6 sessions). After the fix a part PUT takes 3-9 ms CPU (256 MB run) and 1 GiB uploads complete in one session (2026-11-02 runs).
limits.carton: Before: a clear HTTP error, 4 retries with backoff, then a resumable stop that never finished. Fixed by streaming the part body to R2 or the vault (fix/cf-stream-parts).

limits.observed: A 96 MiB part failed 503 while another upload shared the isolate; a 99 MiB part alone passed.
limits.carton: Same retry path; streaming parts (fix/cf-stream-parts) no longer buffers them.

limits.value: 100 MB request body (Free and Pro plans)
limits.observed: A 101 MiB part: 413 at the edge; 64, 96 and 99 MiB passed.
limits.carton: Client parts are 8 MiB by default and at most 64 MiB unless a file passes 640 GiB (10,000 parts).

limits.observed: A raw 33 MiB frame: Cloudflare closes 1009; the room closes 1009 above its own 24 MiB cap.
limits.carton: Changes over 1 MiB go as envelopes through blob storage (5 MiB: 2.0-3.5 s, 20 MiB: 3.9-5.1 s, both hosts); a 30 MiB change is refused locally as too large in 215 ms and the next edit still confirms.

limits.value: 1,000 internal subrequests per request (R2 binding calls; Workers Free), 50 external
limits.observed: blobs/heads with 200 keys ok (4.1 s); 1,000 keys answered 200 per call (9.4 s).
limits.carton: The host answers at most BLOB_HEADS_PER_REQUEST keys per call; the client asks again for the rest.

limits.observed: Not hit: the vault stores 1 MiB chunks.

limits.value: not a Cloudflare limit: a dead link keeps the WebSocket 'open'
limits.observed: Old client: through a 5-minute outage the socket stayed open, status 'Syncing' for 5 min, 0 offline events; resumed only on TCP's retransmission timer (everything settled 66.5 s after the edits ended).
limits.carton: Fixed (fix/cf-dead-link): the transport closes a link whose keepalive goes unanswered for 15 s, and pings on a send after silence.

limits.value: not a Cloudflare limit: Workers Free's 100k requests/day across the account
limits.observed: A client whose session the host refuses retried 86 times a minute (~0.57 s gaps), ~2 Worker requests per try: ~245k/day per stuck client, 2.5x the Free plan's daily requests.
limits.carton: Fixed (fix/cf-reconnect-backoff): exponential backoff with jitter to 15 s, 5 min while the session is refused.

limits.value: Workers 100k requests/day; DO 100k requests, 13,000 GB-s, 5M rows read, 100k rows written per day (Free)
limits.observed: Not hit on purpose: hitting one would take the live showcase site down until 00:00 UTC (same account).
limits.carton: Not measured. The lab's own daily write cap (fix/cf-write-cap) was shown instead: 429 DailyWriteCap with Retry-After and a clear message; the uploader stops resumably.

limits.value: the lab deployments' own cap (fix/cf-write-cap): R2 8 GiB/day, no-R2 4 GiB/day, 20k write calls/day
limits.observed: A 256 MB vault upload after the day's earlier uploads was refused: 429 DailyWriteCap.
limits.carton: Refused before any byte is stored; the client backs off and stops resumably with the server's message.

limits.value: not a Cloudflare limit: DO storage 5 GB (Free), $0.20/GB-month (Paid)
limits.observed: The vault had no sweep for abandoned multipart uploads: a killed 1 GB upload left ~600 MB of parts in the DO for good (dropped by the lab).
limits.carton: Fixed (fix/cf-vault-sweep, deployed to both lab Workers 02:14 UTC): an alarm deletes unfinished uploads untouched for 24 h, 500 rows a pass; not yet exercised live (24 h).

limits.value: workerd cancels a request's work when its client disconnects, unless it is held with ctx.waitUntil (then up to 30 s more)
limits.observed: An uploader killed mid-part: its part request ended 'canceled' in the tail before its finally ran, so the R2 adapter's part lock stayed held for LOCK_TTL_MS (30 min) and 5 resume sessions were refused 'PreconditionFailed: part 33 is being uploaded by another request' (2026-11-02). A 30 s link cut (no disconnect, TCP stalls) was not affected.
limits.carton: Fixed (fix/cf-part-lock): the Worker hands each request's work to waitUntil; after the fix the killed part's request ran on 11.9 s, released its lock, and the upload resumed in one more session.

limits.value: not a Cloudflare limit: Node's happy-eyeballs connect abandons each address after 250 ms (autoSelectFamilyAttemptTimeout, Node 20+)
limits.observed: On the bad profile (~400 ms round trip) every Node fetch, node:https request and WebSocket failed to connect (ETIMEDOUT / UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT); curl connected in 2.0-2.5 s; with the attempt time at 2 s or the selection off a put went through.
limits.carton: Fixed (fix/cf-slow-link-connect): Carton's Node HTTP and WebSocket clients raise the default to at least 2 s; sync and uploads then work on bad.

limits.value: DO rows written: 100k a day (Free); the vault writes ~4,070 per GB uploaded
limits.observed: 3 of 3 vault uploads of 1 GiB wrote exactly 4,370 rows each (a row per MiB written as a part, copied on complete, the part rows deleted).
limits.carton: Without R2, the Free plan's daily rows cap the account's vault uploads at about 24 GB a day (before any edits); the vault sweep adds a row per row it deletes.

limits.value: lab tooling: wrangler tail is best effort
limits.observed: With several runs at once it kept 24-30% of a proxy run's 3,018 requests (no sampling notice printed); with one run at a time it was complete (1.00 per connect, 136 per GiB uploaded).
limits.carton: -  (the lab counts Worker requests with the clients' own counts where they exist)

limits.value: 1 GB in one Durable Object on Free, 10 GB on Paid (Cloudflare's Durable Objects limits page)
limits.observed: Not pushed to the limit. The lab's 1 GiB vault uploads (1.07 GB) completed in one vault on Workers Free (2026-11-01 and 11-02), so the 1 GB wasn't enforced at that size.
limits.carton: Without R2, a project's media all sits in one vault object, so the media it keeps must fit this, on either plan. Past it, writes fail (SQLITE_FULL); reads and deletes still work. Keep media in R2.

limits.value: R2: 10 GB-month of storage, 1 million Class A and 10 million Class B a month free, on either Workers plan
limits.observed: The lab stayed far under it (its R2 use is in CF-VERIFY.md).
limits.carton: Past it, R2 bills; it never stops working. Its free amounts are monthly, not daily.

notes.workersFree: Workers Free: 100,000 requests a day, 10 ms of CPU per request, no fee. Requests to static assets are free and unlimited.
notes.doFree: Durable Objects on Workers Free (SQLite-backed only): 100,000 requests, 13,000 GB-s, 5 million rows read and 100,000 rows written a day; 5 GB stored in total.
notes.ws: A request is needed to create a WebSocket connection. For billing only, a 20:1 ratio is applied to incoming WebSocket messages; outgoing messages and incoming protocol pings aren't charged; auto-responses (setWebSocketAutoResponse) aren't charged.
notes.alarm: Each setAlarm() is billed as a single row written; deletes are counted as rows written.
notes.duration: Duration bills the 128 MB a Durable Object is allocated, whatever it uses; an object that is idle and eligible for hibernation isn't billed for duration.
notes.r2: R2 bills on either Workers plan; its free amounts are monthly and apply to Standard storage only. Storage is the average of each day's peak over the month. Egress is free. DeleteObject and AbortMultipartUpload are free.
notes.dailyReset: Workers Free daily limits reset at 00:00 UTC.
notes.rounding: Durable Objects: "billable usage is the amount consumed in excess of the included monthly allocation. This billable usage is rounded up to the next billable unit" (a million requests, GB-s or rows; a GB-month). R2: "Cloudflare rounds up your usage to the next billing unit" (a million operations, a GB-month). Workers requests and CPU: no rounding documented.
notes.perObject: A SQLite-backed Durable Object holds at most 10 GB on Workers Paid, 1 GB on the Free plan; past it, writes fail (SQLITE_FULL) while reads and deletes still work.
notes.durationShared: Duration is billed in wall-clock time while the object is active, shared across all requests active on it at once.

documentedLimits.value: 1 GB in one Durable Object on Free, 10 GB on Paid (Cloudflare's Durable Objects limits page)
documentedLimits.observed: Not pushed to the limit. The lab's 1 GiB vault uploads (1.07 GB) completed in one vault on Workers Free (2026-11-01 and 11-02), so the 1 GB wasn't enforced at that size.
documentedLimits.carton: Without R2, a project's media all sits in one vault object, so the media it keeps must fit this, on either plan. Past it, writes fail (SQLITE_FULL); reads and deletes still work. Keep media in R2.

documentedLimits.value: R2: 10 GB-month of storage, 1 million Class A and 10 million Class B a month free, on either Workers plan
documentedLimits.observed: The lab stayed far under it (its R2 use is in CF-VERIFY.md).
documentedLimits.carton: Past it, R2 bills; it never stops working. Its free amounts are monthly, not daily.
